**Starts** once #191, #197, #198, and #199 are merged. #59, #56, #182, and #184 are already merged.

#197 runs the coordinator as a named agent. #198 builds how every worker is started and what it returns. #199 adds the workers' tools on the `trip` server. This issue builds the stay researcher on top of them.

## Why

The stay researcher is the first worker. It finds lodging for a stay, and fills the stops near it with candidates, so the coordinator can offer the user choices (technical spec 6.1). It's also the first time the coordinator hands work to another agent.

## Design

- [Technical spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/technical-spec.md), sections 4.2 (fill), 5.3, 6.1, 6.4, and 6.5 (how a worker is started, its brief, its result, and the hooks and settings).
- [Tool design](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/tools.md), sections 1 (the `worker` server), 2.1 (the candidate tools and `read_worker_brief_facts`), 2.6 (`report_result`), and 3.
- [Web search design](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/data-sources/web-search.md).

## Open questions

- ~~What exact fields go in a worker brief and in a worker's result? Technical spec section 5.3 lists the contents, not the fields. Proposed on 2026-10-27: the result goes through a worker tool with a schema, checked by hooks, and the worker reads its brief's facts from code, so the coordinator writes only what needs its judgment. #182 says the pattern in full, and checks it against the SDK.~~ **Moved on 2026-10-27 to #191,** which designs the worker's setup from what #182 found.
- ~~Can a session resume when its transcript ends in a worker call that never got its result? A restart can leave it that way. If the SDK won't resume, the transcript adapter (`src/persistence/transcript-adapter.ts`) drops the unfinished line. #182 checks it.~~ **Settled on 2026-10-27 in PR #189:** the SDK resumes as is, and adds a result saying the call was interrupted, so the transcript adapter needs no change. #191 writes it into persistence design section 7.
- ~~May a worker run in the background? Each subagent definition has a `background` option. In a check in PR #23, a background helper finished after the coordinator's turn ended, and the SDK started a second turn on its own, in the same `query()` call. Raised in PR #23. #136 found that the `Agent` tool itself runs a worker in the background unless the model sets its `run_in_background` input to `false`. With two workers, the coordinator left it out. `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS=1`, in the Claude Code process's environment, keeps every worker in the foreground, and two still ran at the same time ([research/agent-evaluations.md](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/research/agent-evaluations.md), section 2.7, once PR #138 merges). #182 finds the setting that keeps workers in the foreground.~~ **Settled on 2026-10-27 in PR #189:** no. A background worker's own text skips the result pattern. `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS=1` keeps every worker in the foreground. #191 writes it into the design.
- ~~Meal coverage: recommend every meal, or only lunch and dinner by default? It depends on data quality. From the functional spec. Moved from open item 1 in the development plan.~~ **Settled on 2026-10-27 in chat:** by default, the coordinator gives each day a lunch stop and a dinner stop. On a driving day, lunch is along the leg. Breakfast gets a stop only when the trip brief's meal preferences say local breakfast, not hotel breakfast. Anything the user asks for changes the default, such as "we'll picnic on the drive" or pie at Gifford Homestead, saved to trip memory for this trip or user memory for a standing habit. A fixed default makes a trip with the same brief get the same meals, so a missing meal in a trace is a bug or a user request, not a model choice. It costs a card for every lunch and dinner, which is accepted, since choosing where to eat is a big part of a road trip. When a worker finds fewer than three good places, it adds the ones it found and says so in its result. When it finds none, the coordinator tells the user. Write it into technical spec 5.2, under laying out a day, and functional spec 7.3.
- ~~What does each budget tier, value, mid-range, and posh, mean? The coordinator's instructions name the tiers but don't say. Functional spec 7.1 says the agent infers a place's tier from descriptions, reviews, and price signals, such as "$$", but not where one tier ends and the next starts. The stay researcher is the first agent that picks places by tier. Raised while going through the coordinator's view file, `src/agent/coordinator.view.md`.~~ More, raised by Joe on 2026-10-27 from the Natick to Bar Harbor trip (session `session_5hf47qpn`): **Settled on 2026-10-27 in chat,** in the parts below. #184 makes a tier a label on each place, not a target, and #60 builds on it.
  - ~~A tier can't be a dollar amount, since a posh hotel in Ohio may cost less than a value one in San Francisco. A proposal to weigh: a tier is where a place sits among comparable places in its area, described by the experience rather than price. Value is simple and clean, such as a chain motel or counter service. Mid-range is comfortable and full service, such as a typical sit-down restaurant. Posh is the best the area offers, such as a boutique hotel or a chef-driven restaurant that needs a reservation.~~ **Settled on 2026-10-27 in chat:** A tier is a label on each place, not a target. #184 makes the change: it defines each tier by what staying or eating there is like, has the worker label each lodging and meal candidate with its own tier, and drops the stored tier and rule on stays and meal stops. A worker aims for what the user's own words in its brief say. For #60: `add_lodging_candidates` and `add_stop_candidates` take a required tier for each lodging or meal candidate, judged by the worker. When the area has nothing that fits the brief, such as upscale lodging in Torrey, the worker offers the closest it finds, labeled with their real tier, and says so in its result, and the coordinator tells the user. **How a worker searches.** `search_near` sends the worker's words to Google as written, ranked by how well places match them, so a search for "restaurant" returns whatever is popular nearby. The stay researcher's instructions say to put words in the query that fit what the brief asks for, such as "fine dining" or "boutique hotel" for upscale, "diner" or "budget motel" for value, or "lobster shack"; to search again with other words when the results don't fit; and, for the area's best, to try web search and look each place up with `find_place`. It reports that nothing fits only after more than one search. A price-level filter and a second page of results stay out for now (tool design 2.3), and can be added if evaluations show workers missing good places.
  - ~~Joe doesn't want to label hotels and restaurants by hand, and doesn't want tiers left wholly to the model's judgment. An evaluation could check consistency instead of right answers: does a restaurant's tier agree with Google's price level where there is one, are a town's posh candidates never at a lower price level than its value ones, and does the same place get the same tier across runs? A user's "Higher tier" or "Lower tier" on a card is also a sign that a tier missed for them.~~ **Moved on 2026-10-27 to #185,** an evaluation that checks the stay researcher's tiers for consistency, scored in code: price level, order within a town, and the same tier across runs. The clicks aren't used, since there are too few.
  - ~~Users mean different things by the same tier, so the user's own words may matter more than the tier. Technical spec section 4 says a worker gets the tier and a short rule, "never the rule text." In that trip, the coordinator gave the Camden stay the rule "upscale hotel or B&B in Camden," which says the tier again plus a lodging preference, "B&B," that a stay has nowhere else to hold. Other rules only said the tier again in words, such as "meals upscale or posh." So: should a worker get the user's own words with the tier, and where does a stay's lodging preference, such as a B&B, belong?~~ **Partly settled on 2026-10-27 in chat:** a worker gets the user's own words that apply, for budget, meals, and lodging, in place of a tier and a rule. The coordinator can add its own reading where a rule is clear. #184 writes it into technical spec 5.3.
  - ~~Where does a stay's lodging preference belong, such as "a B&B could be a good option in one of them" on the Bar Harbor trip? Today a stay has nowhere to hold it, so the coordinator put it in the tier rule, which #184 removes.~~ **Settled on 2026-10-27 in chat:** the trip brief's budget item is replaced by a lodging preferences item, in the user's words, beside meal preferences, and the B&B wish goes there. Spending on food goes in meal preferences. A lodging wish that comes up later in chat goes in trip memory. The coordinator passes the preferences and memory that apply into each worker brief, and keeps track of a wish that covers more than one stay. "Hotels only" includes B&Bs and inns listed on Google. #184 makes the change.
- ~~How are the stay researcher's turns traced in Phoenix? #135 traces only the coordinator, with spans from our own code. By default, the Agent SDK sends the coordinator only a subagent's tool calls and results, not its text or thinking. Whether its stream events come through, with its tokens, needs checking ([research/agent-evaluations.md](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/research/agent-evaluations.md), section 3). Raised on 2026-10-25, while writing #135.~~ Moved to #136 on 2026-10-25.
- ~~How do the workers get `search_near` and `search_along_leg`? #59 added both tools, but put them on no MCP server. The coordinator's places server (`createPlacesServer()` in `src/tools/places-server.ts`) holds only `find_place` and `read_place`, so the coordinator doesn't see the searches. The SDK's subagents share the main query's MCP servers unless an `AgentDefinition` gives its own `mcpServers`, and the coordinator's `allowedTools` likely only refuses a call to a tool it sees, rather than hiding it (not checked). So the stay researcher likely needs its own places server, with `find_place` and `search_near`, and the leg scout (#61) one with `search_along_leg` too. Raised on 2026-10-26, in PR #159. #182 checks a worker's own server, and which tools the coordinator sees.~~ **Moved on 2026-10-27 to #191.**
- ~~What do the stay researcher's instructions say about each field the candidate tools take? Their input descriptions give only the format (tool design section 4), so what each means goes in the instructions: `howFound`, which is "google" for a place found with `search_near`, and "webSearch" for one found by web search and then looked up with `find_place`; `sourceLink`, the place's Google Maps link from the search result, or the web page's link; the rationale, one or two sentences on why the place fits, never naming the trip's dates (technical spec 6.4); `notes`, given as "" when there are none; and `visitTimeInMinutes`, the worker's own estimate. #199 built the tools, and tool design 2.1 has what they take. Raised on 2026-10-28, while #199 was being built.~~ **Settled on 2026-10-28 in chat:** the instructions say this about each field:
  - **`howFound` and `sourceLink` go together.** "google" goes with the place's Google Maps link, the first link on its "Links:" line in the search result. "webSearch" goes with the page's link, when a web page is what led the worker to the place, which it then looked up with `find_place`. When a place turned up both ways, the web page wins, since the option card links to it, and a page such as Atlas Obscura's tells the user more than a Maps pin.
  - **The rationale** is one or two sentences on why this place fits this stop, tied to the user's words in the worker brief, such as "Walkable to the barbecue spots." It doesn't repeat what the card already shows, such as the rating, price level, or tier. It never names the trip's dates or nights.
  - **Notes** are practical things to know before going, such as "closed Mondays", "reservations advised", or "cash only", or "" when there are none. A clash with the trip's dates, such as "closed Wednesdays, and Day 4 is a Wednesday", goes in `report_result` as a problem, not in the notes.
  - **`visitTimeInMinutes`** is the worker's estimate of the time spent at the place, not the drive there, sized to what the user cares about. A hiker at Arches' Windows section might get 90, and a quick look 30. The day's schedule is built from it, so a realistic time beats a short one. No data source gives a visit time, so it stays the model's own judgment, and gets tuned once we see how it works.

  The leg scout (#61) takes the same fields, so this is one block of instruction text it can reuse word for word. The domain model's rationale example, "Walkable to the barbecue spots, fits mid-range.", drops "fits mid-range", since that repeats the tier.
- ~~**What do the workers' instructions say a problem and a question are, for `report_result`?** Tool design 2.6 says a problem is something the coordinator should know, and a question needs the user's decision, since a worker can't ask the user anything. #198 left that out of the tool's description, since what an item means goes in the instructions (tool design section 4). Proposed: one block of instruction text, with the examples from tool design 2.6, that the leg scout (#61) and the weather worker (#64) reuse word for word. Raised on 2026-10-28, while #198 was being built.~~ **Settled on 2026-10-28, in #60's PR:** one block of instruction text, `PROBLEMS_AND_QUESTIONS` in `src/agent/worker-instructions.ts`, that every worker's instructions include word for word. A problem is something the coordinator should know that it can't tell from what the worker saved, such as a closure on the trip's dates, fewer than three places that fit, or nothing at the tier the worker brief asked for. A question needs the user's decision, and the worker asks one only when it can't do an item well without the answer. Each is a short sentence that names stops and stays as the tools do. The worker doesn't list what it saved, or say that all went well, and gives empty lists when there's nothing to report. Technical spec 6.4 has the text.

## Do

- Add the stay researcher's instructions.
- Write what the instructions say about each candidate field (the settled question above) as one block that the leg scout (#61) can reuse word for word. Change the domain model's rationale example to "Walkable to the barbecue spots." wherever it appears in `design/`.
- Give the stay researcher a definition as technical spec 6.5 says, with the type `stay-researcher` and its tools from tool design section 3. Add its view file, and list its type's description and tools in the coordinator's view (DEVELOPMENT.md section 5).
- Draft the worker brief's outline (technical spec 5.3), for Joe to review in the PR. #198 drafts the result's wording.
- Give the coordinator `Agent(stay-researcher)`, so the stay researcher is the only agent type it can start (technical spec 6.5).
- Add the coordinator's instructions for the fill round. They include what each worker brief carries from the user's meal and lodging preferences, interests, and memory, and how the coordinator keeps track of a wish that covers more than one stay (technical spec 5.3 and section 9). #184 wrote those into the design, but left them out of the prompt, since there were no workers yet.
- Add the sentence from technical spec 5.2's bullet on a stay that moves to a different town that needs workers, which #55 left out. It goes after the hotel sentence that #56 adds to the "Changes to stays" section in `src/agent/coordinator-prompt.ts`. Word for word: "Then send workers for any lodging or stop whose candidates no longer fit."

## Done when

In a chat with the coordinator:

- On the Moab trip (domain model, section 5.2), with lodging preferences that ask for a comfortable mid-range hotel, the stay researcher adds three lodging candidates that fit, each labeled with its tier, and fills the stops near the Moab stay.
- The coordinator sees one line per candidate, not full records.
- The coordinator's `Agent` tool offers the stay researcher and no other agent type.
- ~~The answer to the resume question above is checked, and written into persistence design section 7.~~ Done in #191.

## Ends in

A PR.

**Settled in:** chat. Propose each answer to Joe in chat first, and write it in once he agrees.

---

Moved from the [development plan](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/plan/development-plan.md#phase-27-the-stay-researcher).
